assessment.title: Claude Pro Assessment
assessment.description: Tests whether you can pick the right Claude surface for a task, predict failure modes, and roll Claude out across a team without it generating expensive nonsense.

questions.stem: Your PM asks Claude.ai for the latest RBI guidelines on co-branded credit cards. Claude confidently cites three circulars. What is the single biggest risk?

choices.label: Without web search turned on, Claude will confidently produce circular numbers that look real but were never issued
choices.explanation: This is the classic recency-and-citation hallucination. Without a tool that actually fetches the RBI website, Claude pattern-matches to plausible circular numbers. Always turn on web search for regulatory work.

choices.label: Claude.ai has a 200K token limit and the circulars do not fit
choices.explanation: Opus 4.7 has a 1M context window in 2026. Context size is not the failure mode here.

choices.label: The PM should have used Claude Haiku 4.5 because it is faster
choices.explanation: Speed is irrelevant; correctness and citation are the problem. Switching to Haiku makes hallucinations cheaper, not rarer.

choices.label: Claude refuses to discuss banking regulation
choices.explanation: It does not refuse. The problem is that it answers too willingly without grounding.

questions.stem: Pick the two scenarios where Claude Code clearly beats Claude.ai pasted-in code.

choices.label: Refactoring 14 files that all import the same util
choices.explanation: Multi-file edits with grep, read and apply-patch tools are exactly Claude Code's strength. Claude.ai cannot touch your filesystem.

choices.label: Asking what a regex does
choices.explanation: A one-shot question with no file access is faster on Claude.ai.

choices.label: Running a migration script and verifying the output across three environments
choices.explanation: Background tasks plus shell access plus a CLAUDE.md kernel make Claude Code the right tool. You want it to actually run things and check, not describe what it would run.

choices.label: Drafting a one-paragraph PR description
choices.explanation: That is a single text task. Claude.ai or even Haiku will do it cheaper.

questions.stem: A junior PM at your Bengaluru fintech sends a Slack message to the CEO that begins 'As an AI language model, I would like to thank you for the opportunity'. What broke?

choices.label: The no-send-without-review rule was skipped — the draft was copied verbatim
choices.explanation: Claude is a draft engine, not the sender. Every output goes through a human read before it leaves your name.

choices.label: Claude Sonnet 4.6 has a known bug with Slack formatting
choices.explanation: It does not. The bug is the workflow.

choices.label: The PM should have used Opus instead of Sonnet
choices.explanation: Bigger model would still produce the same opener if asked badly. The model is not the issue; the review gate is.

choices.label: Slack stripped the formatting and revealed the AI prefix
choices.explanation: Slack does not add AI disclaimers. The text was already there.

questions.stem: What is the best opening move when using Claude for design critique on a new dashboard mockup?

choices.label: Upload the mockup, name the user, name the goal, and ask Claude to find the three weakest decisions before suggesting fixes
choices.explanation: Critique-not-generate. You constrain Claude to find weaknesses with a named user and goal so it cannot drift into generic advice.

choices.label: Ask Claude to redesign the dashboard from scratch
choices.explanation: This loses everything you know. Claude will produce a generic SaaS template and erase the constraints you have already considered.

choices.label: Ask Claude what colour to use for the primary CTA
choices.explanation: Too narrow. You will get a confident answer with no understanding of contrast, brand, or context.

choices.label: Paste the Figma file into Claude.ai
choices.explanation: Figma URLs do not render. The mockup needs to be an image or a structured description.

questions.stem: Which two are real built-in Claude Code subagents you would invoke with the Task tool?

choices.label: Plan
choices.explanation: Plan is a built-in subagent that does read-only investigation and writes a plan to docs/PLAN.md.

choices.label: general-purpose
choices.explanation: general-purpose is the catch-all subagent for multi-step search and research with its own context window.

choices.label: auto-deploy
choices.explanation: There is no built-in deploy subagent. Deployment is intentionally human-driven.

choices.label: money-mover
choices.explanation: Made up. No financial subagent exists.

questions.stem: You are running Claude Code on a 200-file refactor. After 40 minutes it has touched 60 files and is still going. What is the right move?

choices.label: Stop, ask it to write a plan, split the work into parallel subagents with bounded scope, and resume
choices.explanation: Long unsupervised loops are where Claude drifts. Bound the scope, fan out, and recheck artifacts at the boundaries.

choices.label: Let it keep going — it has momentum
choices.explanation: Momentum is the warning sign. The longer it runs unchecked, the more likely the last 30 files were applied to a wrong assumption.

choices.label: Switch to Opus mid-run for higher quality
choices.explanation: Switching models mid-run loses cache and does not fix the lack of plan.

choices.label: Cancel everything and do it manually
choices.explanation: Premature surrender. Bound and resume; do not throw away the first 60 files of work.

questions.stem: A CA firm in Pune wants Claude to read 800 ITRs and flag anomalies. Which surface and pattern fits best?

choices.label: Anthropic API with batch processing on Haiku 4.5, structured JSON output, with a 2 percent human sample review
choices.explanation: High-volume, structured, repetitive work belongs on the API with the cheapest model that holds quality. Always sample. Never assume 100 percent correctness.

choices.label: Paste each ITR into Claude.ai one by one with Opus
choices.explanation: 800 manual paste cycles costs partner-level hours. Wrong tool.

choices.label: Drop the PDFs into a Claude Project and ask one big question
choices.explanation: Projects help with shared context, not 800 individual document analyses with structured output.

choices.label: Use Claude Code to write a Python script that calls Sonnet 4.6 sequentially
choices.explanation: Closer, but sequential calls on Sonnet are 10x more expensive and slower than batched Haiku, with no quality gain on a structured-extraction task.

questions.stem: Which two belong in a CLAUDE.md kernel file?

choices.label: Hard rules with MUST / SHOULD / MAY priority
choices.explanation: Hard rules at the top means Claude reads them every session. This is the whole point of a kernel file.

choices.label: Slash commands and when to use each
choices.explanation: Slash commands collapse repeated protocols ('plan', 'bugfix', 'ship') into one token instead of pasted prose.

choices.label: Production database credentials
choices.explanation: Never. Secrets in CLAUDE.md is a security failure waiting to happen and most editors auto-include it.

choices.label: A daily TODO list
choices.explanation: The kernel is durable rules. TODOs go in PLAN.md or your tracker, not in a file every session reads.

questions.stem: You ask Claude to draft a client proposal. It returns 1,800 polished words. What is the right next step?

choices.label: Read every paragraph, cut at least 30 percent, and replace at least three sentences in your own voice
choices.explanation: Length is the lazy signal of effort. Cut, sharpen, claim it. Otherwise it reads as Claude and the client smells it.

choices.label: Send it as is — it is well written
choices.explanation: This is the no-send-without-review failure. Polish does not equal voice or accuracy.

choices.label: Ask Claude to make it longer
choices.explanation: More length, more drift, more chance of fabrication. Wrong direction.

choices.label: Run it through Claude again to detect AI
choices.explanation: AI detectors on AI output are theatre. The fix is your editing pass, not another model call.

questions.stem: A team uses Claude Code with run_in_background for a 3-hour data backfill. What artifact should the background job write?

choices.label: A timestamped log file plus a structured summary so the foreground agent can pick up without rereading 50K lines
choices.explanation: Artifact handoff: long jobs leave a small structured artifact for the next agent to consume. This is the only way fan-out scales.

choices.label: Nothing — the foreground agent will read the full stdout
choices.explanation: 50K lines of stdout will exhaust context and bury the signal. Always summarise to an artifact.

choices.label: An email to the team
choices.explanation: Email is not an agent-readable artifact. The next Claude run cannot use it.

choices.label: A push notification
choices.explanation: Notifications are for humans, not for agent handoff.

questions.stem: Your designer wants Claude to generate 12 hero-image options for a landing page. What is the best framing?

choices.label: Skip image generation in Claude — describe 12 directions, then commission three from a real image tool
choices.explanation: Claude does not generate images. The right Claude move is to brainstorm directions and constrain the prompt for an image model.

choices.label: Ask Claude to render 12 hero images directly
choices.explanation: Claude does not produce images. Asking will return 12 text descriptions or apologies.

choices.label: Ask Claude for 12 colour palettes
choices.explanation: Different question. Palettes do not solve the hero-image need.

choices.label: Ask Claude to copy 12 competitor heroes
choices.explanation: Imitation is not the brief and Claude cannot pull live competitor pages without web search.

questions.stem: Pick two real failure modes of long-running Claude workflows.

choices.label: Drift — by step 20, Claude is solving a slightly different problem than step 1
choices.explanation: Drift is the headline failure mode of unsupervised loops. Restate the goal at every checkpoint.

choices.label: Cascade — one wrong assumption gets reused in 14 downstream files
choices.explanation: Cascade is why bounded scope and artifact handoff matter. One bad assumption multiplies.

choices.label: Claude refusing to run for more than 5 minutes
choices.explanation: There is no such ceiling. Run length is a budget choice, not a hard limit.

choices.label: Claude logging out of itself
choices.explanation: Made up. Sessions persist.

questions.stem: Claude Sonnet 4.6 in 2026 costs roughly $3 per million input tokens. You run a workflow at 400K tokens of input per task and run it 200 times a week. Roughly what is your weekly bill?

choices.label: About $240 a week
choices.explanation: 400K x 200 = 80M input tokens. 80 x $3 = $240. Output tokens add more, but the input dominates here.

choices.label: About $24 a week
choices.explanation: Off by a factor of 10. Easy to make on the back of a napkin. Recompute the input volume.

choices.label: About $2,400 a week
choices.explanation: Off by a factor of 10 the other way. Probably you confused tokens with characters.

choices.label: Free if you have a Pro plan
choices.explanation: Pro plan is the chat product, not the API. API usage is metered separately.

questions.stem: You are rolling Claude out across a 200-person company. Where should you start?

choices.label: Pick one team with a measurable, low-risk workflow, run a 30-day pilot with eval and review gates, then expand
choices.explanation: Pilots prove value and surface failure modes before they hit 200 people. Eval and review gates are non-negotiable for any roll-out.

choices.label: Buy seats for everyone and announce it on Slack
choices.explanation: Mass roll-out without a pilot is how you end up in newspapers about an AI mistake.

choices.label: Mandate Claude for every Slack message
choices.explanation: Forcing the tool over-rotates and creates worse output where humans were already fine.

choices.label: Wait until someone proves ROI
choices.explanation: Nobody will, because nobody has a budget. You design the pilot.

questions.stem: Claude.ai Projects let you attach a knowledge base for repeated reuse. What is the right material to put in?

choices.label: Your style guide, last 6 months of polished examples, and your refusal list
choices.explanation: Projects shine when the same context is reused. Style + examples + 'never say this' is the trio.

choices.label: Every PDF on the company drive
choices.explanation: Volume kills relevance. Curate.

choices.label: Customer credit card numbers
choices.explanation: Never. PII in a Project is a leakage waiting to happen.

choices.label: Just one file with today's date
choices.explanation: Then a Project is wasted; a normal chat would do.

questions.stem: Pick two cases where you should NOT use Claude.

choices.label: Real-time stock prices for a trading decision
choices.explanation: Even with web search, latency and reliability are wrong for trading. Use a market data API directly.

choices.label: Drafting a Slack standup
choices.explanation: This is a perfect Claude task — short, low risk, one human review.

choices.label: Diagnosing a specific patient's medication interaction without doctor review
choices.explanation: Health decisions at the individual level need licensed review. Claude is a research aide, not a clinician.

choices.label: Summarising a 60-page RFP
choices.explanation: Long-document summarisation is a core Claude strength.

questions.stem: MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects Claude to external tools. Which is the safest thing to expose first?

choices.label: Read-only access to your wiki and design system
choices.explanation: Read-only first lets Claude be more useful with zero blast radius. Add write access only after you trust the loop.

choices.label: Write access to production database
choices.explanation: Catastrophic first move. A confident wrong query drops a table.

choices.label: Email send permissions
choices.explanation: An autonomous loop sending emails on your behalf is the no-send-without-review rule violated at scale.

choices.label: Stripe charge endpoint
choices.explanation: Charging cards is exactly the kind of action you do not want a model to do unsupervised.

project.title: Capstone: Roll Out Claude Across a 200-Person Company in 30 Days
project.prompt:
Your CEO has read a McKinsey report on the flight back from Davos and now wants Claude rolled out across the entire 200-person company by end of next month. Budget is approved. She wants you to scope the 30-day pilot.

You have four candidate verticals: **cowork** (Slack, email, meetings), **code** (engineering team of 40), **design** (product design team of 8), and **orchestration** (long-running workflows in ops, finance, support).

Pick **three** of the four to include in the pilot. Skip one. Defend the choice.

For each of the three you pick, deliver:

1. **Specific workflow** — name one concrete task that Claude will replace or augment. Not 'help with email'; say 'draft first-pass replies to support tickets in Zendesk for the L1 team to review and send'.
2. **Surface and model** — Claude.ai Project, Claude Code, or API. Which model and why. Approximate weekly cost in dollars.
3. **Eval** — how you will measure whether it worked. One leading metric, one lagging metric, one failure metric.
4. **Failure mode** — the most likely way this goes wrong, and what you will see when it does.
5. **Human review gate** — what cannot ship without a human. Be specific.

For the vertical you skipped, write 80-120 words explaining why it is wrong **for this company at this stage**. Generic answers ('it's risky') do not score.

At the bottom, give the CEO a one-paragraph executive summary she can forward to the board. Then add a single bullet titled **'What I would do differently if budget was half'** — because budgets always get cut.

levels.label: Each pick is justified with a workflow, surface, model and weekly cost; the skipped vertical has a company-specific reason; eval has leading + lagging + failure metric
Picks are justified but missing one of: cost, eval failure metric, or the skip rationale is generic
Picks are vibes-based or two of the above are missing
Recommendations clearly account for the 200-person size, the four verticals' different risk profiles, and Indian tech context (compliance, data residency, cost in INR)
Acknowledges company size and risk but ignores India-specific or compliance-specific constraints
Same generic answer would apply to any company, any country, any size
Executive summary is one paragraph, board-ready; rubric items are short and skimmable; the budget-cut bullet shows real prioritisation
Mostly clear but executive summary buries the lead, or budget-cut bullet just removes the cheapest item
Wall of text, no executive summary, or budget-cut bullet is missing

credential.title: Claude Pro: Cowork, Code, Design
credential.description: Holder can pick the right Claude surface for a task, drive Claude Code with a CLAUDE.md kernel and subagents, and roll Claude out across a team with eval and human-review gates.
